intro: A fun 10-minute journey around Kerala, India and the world. Tap, explore, then take the Daily Brain Spark quiz!

slides.title: Kerala keeps building its healthcare network
slides.summary: Kerala’s health system is in the news today as the state continues work on strengthening public healthcare services and access.
slides.fun: Healthcare stories help us understand how hospitals, doctors and public services support communities.

slides.title: Medicine availability matters
slides.summary: Keeping essential medicines available in government hospitals is an important part of making public healthcare work smoothly.
slides.fun: A medicine supply chain means checking what is needed, what is in stock and where supplies should go.

slides.title: Kerala watches weather and water
slides.summary: Weather, rainfall and water management remain important topics for Kerala because they affect farming, travel and everyday life.
slides.fun: Kerala’s long coastline, rivers and monsoon climate make weather science especially interesting here.

slides.title: Great Indian Bustards return to the wild
slides.summary: Two male Great Indian Bustards were released into Rajasthan’s Desert National Park as part of efforts to rebuild this endangered bird population.
slides.fun: The Great Indian Bustard is one of India’s most threatened large birds. Conservation breeding can help increase its numbers.

slides.title: Three scientists win the Nobel Prize in Medicine
slides.summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries behind optogenetics.
slides.fun: Optogenetics uses light to control specific cells, giving scientists a powerful way to study how the brain works.

slides.title: Cricket records keep making news
slides.summary: India’s cricket season continues to produce major performances, including Virat Kohli reaching 15,000 runs in 50-over cricket.
slides.fun: Reaching 15,000 runs in one-day cricket is an enormous milestone requiring years of consistent performance.

slides.title: India–US trade talks face a difficult moment
slides.summary: India’s Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said India–US trade negotiations had reached a plateau, with tariffs and market access among the issues.
slides.fun: Trade talks are negotiations about how countries buy and sell goods and services to each other.

slides.title: School protests make news in France
slides.summary: Large student protests in France have focused on school conditions, teacher shortages and education pressures.
slides.fun: Around the world, students and teachers sometimes speak up when they think education systems need changes.

slides.title: World science and sports stay busy
slides.summary: Today’s international news includes developments in science, sport, technology and global cooperation.
slides.fun: Following several different topics helps us see how connected countries and people are.

quiz.q: What endangered Indian bird was released into Rajasthan’s Desert National Park?
quiz.why: Two male Great Indian Bustards were released as part of conservation efforts.

quiz.q: What did the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine recognise?
quiz.why: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were recognised for discoveries that laid the foundation of optogenetics.

quiz.q: Which Indian cricketer reached 15,000 runs in 50-over cricket?
quiz.why: Virat Kohli became the second player after Sachin Tendulkar to reach 15,000 runs in the 50-over format.

quiz.q: What did India’s Finance Minister say about India–US trade talks?
options: They had moved to a sports agreement
quiz.why: Reuters reported that Nirmala Sitharaman said the negotiations had reached a plateau.

quiz.q: In which country were large student protests about school conditions reported today?
quiz.why: Reports from France described large student protests focused on education conditions.

quiz.q: Why is medicine availability important in government hospitals?
options: It helps patients receive needed treatment
quiz.why: Reliable medicine supplies help hospitals provide appropriate treatment to patients.
